# Vectors and matrices

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Quiver

`enum Quiver` — Quiver: A Swift package for statistics, linear algebra, and machine learning *(since 1.1.0)*

- `static let version: String` — Library version. Keep in sync with the package tag at release time. *(since 1.1.0)*

## Array extensions where Element: Numeric

- `func dot(_ other: [Element]) -> Element` — Calculates the dot product of two vectors. Returns: The scalar dot product of the two vectors
- `func transformedBy(_ matrix: [[Element]]) -> [Element]` — Transforms this vector using a matrix (matrix-vector multiplication). Returns: The transformed vector
- `func info() -> String` — Returns a summary of the array including count, type, and a preview of elements. Returns: A formatted string summarizing the array
- `func reshaped(rows: Int, columns: Int) -> [[Element]]` — Reshapes a one-dimensional array into a two-dimensional matrix with the specified dimensions using row-major order. Returns: A two-dimensional array with the specified shape.

## Array extensions where Element.Element: Numeric, Element: Collection

- `func transpose() -> [[Element.Element]]` — Returns the transpose of a matrix Returns: A new matrix where rows become columns and columns become rows
- `func transposed() -> [[Element.Element]]` — Returns the transpose of a matrix (convenience method matching Swift naming conventions) Returns: A new matrix where rows become columns and columns become rows
- `func column(at index: Element.Index) -> [Element.Element]` — Extracts a column from a matrix at the specified index Returns: An array containing all elements from the specified column
- `func transform(_ vector: [Element.Element]) -> [Element.Element]` — Transforms a vector by this matrix (matrix-vector multiplication) Returns: The transformed vector
- `func multiplyMatrix(_ other: [[Element.Element]]) -> [[Element.Element]]` — Multiplies this matrix by another matrix to compose transformations. Returns: The resulting composed transformation matrix
- `var shape: (rows: Int, columns: Int) { get }` — Returns the shape of a two-dimensional array as a `(rows, columns)` tuple. Returns: A tuple of `(rows: Int, columns: Int)`. Returns `(0, 0)` for an empty matrix.
- `var size: Int { get }` — Returns the total number of elements across all dimensions. Returns: The total element count. Returns `0` for an empty matrix.
- `func flattened() -> [Element.Element]` — Flattens a two-dimensional matrix into a one-dimensional array by concatenating rows in row-major order. Returns: A one-dimensional array containing all matrix elements in row-major order. Returns an empty array if the matrix is empty.
- `func reshaped(rows: Int, columns: Int) -> [[Element.Element]]` — Reshapes a matrix to new dimensions, preserving all elements in row-major order. Returns: A two-dimensional array with the specified shape.

## Array extensions where Element.Element: FloatingPoint, Element: Collection

- `var determinant: Element.Element { get }` — Returns the determinant of a square matrix. Returns: The determinant value
- `func inverted() throws -> [[Element.Element]]` — Returns the inverse of a square matrix. Returns: The inverted matrix Throws: `MatrixError.notSquare` if the matrix is not square, `MatrixError.singular` if the matrix is singular.

## Array extensions where Element == [Double]

- `var determinant: Double { get }` — Returns the determinant of a square matrix. Returns: The determinant value *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var logDeterminant: LogDeterminant { get }` — Returns the sign and natural logarithm of the absolute determinant. Returns: A `LogDeterminant` containing the sign (-1, 0, or 1) and log of the absolute determinant
- `var conditionNumber: Double { get }` — Returns the condition number of the matrix using the 1-norm. Returns: The 1-norm condition number, or `.infinity` for singular matrices
- `func areValidVectorDimensions() -> Bool` — Returns whether all vectors in the collection have the same dimension count. Used to validate that a collection of vectors can be used together in mathematical operations.
- `func averaged() -> [Double]?` — Calculates the element-wise average of a collection of vectors. Returns: A vector where each element is the mean across all input vectors, or `nil` if the array is empty or vectors have inconsistent dimensions
- `func cosineSimilarities(to target: [Double]) -> [Double]` — Calculates cosine similarity between each vector in the array and a target vector. Returns: An array of similarity scores in the range [-1, 1], one per vector
- `func findDuplicates(threshold: Double = 0.95) -> [(index1: Int, index2: Int, similarity: Double)]` — Find pairs of vectors with similarity above the specified threshold. Returns: Array of tuples containing pair indices and similarity scores, sorted by similarity (highest first)
- `func clusterCohesion() -> Double` — Calculate average pairwise similarity as a measure of cluster cohesion. Returns: Average pairwise similarity (0.0 to 1.0), or 0.0 if fewer than 2 vectors
- `func info() -> String` — Returns a statistical summary of a 2D matrix including shape, size, type, and aggregate statistics computed across all elements. Returns: A formatted string summarizing the matrix with shape and statistics

## Array extensions where Element: FloatingPoint

- `var magnitude: Element { get }` — Calculates the magnitude (length) of the vector.
- `var normalized: [Element] { get }` — Returns a normalized version of the vector (unit vector). Returns: A new array with the same direction and magnitude 1.0, or a zero vector if the original has zero magnitude
- `func distance(to other: [Element]) -> Element` — Calculates the Euclidean distance between two points or vectors. Returns: The Euclidean distance between the two vectors
- `func distance(to other: [Element], metric: DistanceMetric) -> Element` — Calculates the distance between two vectors using the given metric. Returns: The distance between the two vectors under the chosen metric *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func cosineOfAngle(with other: [Element]) -> Element` — Returns the cosine of the angle between two vectors. Returns: The cosine of the angle between the two vectors, in the range [-1, 1]
- `func correlation(with other: [Element]) -> Element?` — Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient between two vectors. Returns: The Pearson correlation coefficient, in the range [-1, 1], or `nil` if the result is undefined *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func scalarProjection(onto vector: [Element]) -> Element` — Calculates the scalar projection of this vector onto another vector. Returns: The scalar length of the projection along the target vector's direction
- `func vectorProjection(onto vector: [Element]) -> [Element]` — Calculates the vector projection of this vector onto another vector. Returns: A new vector pointing in the direction of the target with the projected magnitude
- `func orthogonalComponent(to vector: [Element]) -> [Element]` — Returns the component of this vector that is perpendicular to another vector. Returns: A new vector perpendicular to the reference vector
- `func info() -> String` — Returns a statistical summary of the array including count, type, mean, standard deviation, min, and max. Returns: A formatted string summarizing the array with statistics

## Array extensions where Element == Double

- `func distance(to other: [Double], metric: DistanceMetric) -> Double` — Measures the distance between two `[Double]` vectors under the chosen metric. Returns: The distance between the two vectors under the chosen metric. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func topIndices(k: Int) -> [(rank: Int, index: Int, score: Double)]` — Returns the indices and values of the top K highest elements. Returns: Array of tuples containing rank (1-based), index, and score, sorted by score (highest first)
- `func topIndices<T>(k: Int, labels: [T]) -> [(rank: Int, label: T, score: Double)]` — Returns the top K highest scores with corresponding labels. Returns: Array of tuples containing rank (1-based), label, and score, sorted by score (highest first)
- `func sortedIndices() -> [Int]` — Returns the indices that would sort the array in ascending order. Returns: Array of indices representing the sorted order
- `func angle(with other: [Double]) -> Double` — Returns the angle between two vectors in radians. Returns: The angle in radians, in the range [0, π]
- `func angleInDegrees(with other: [Double]) -> Double` — Returns the angle between two vectors in degrees. Returns: The angle in degrees, in the range [0, 180]

## Array extensions where Element == [Float]

- `func cosineSimilarities(to target: [Float]) -> [Float]` — Calculates cosine similarity between each vector in the array and a target vector. Returns: An array of similarity scores in the range [-1, 1], one per vector

## Array extensions where Element == Float

- `func angle(with other: [Float]) -> Float` — Returns the angle between two vectors in radians. Returns: The angle in radians, in the range [0, π]
- `func angleInDegrees(with other: [Float]) -> Float` — Returns the angle between two vectors in degrees. Returns: The angle in degrees, in the range [0, 180]

## Array extensions where Element: Comparable

- `func isEqual(to other: [Element]) -> [Bool]` — Checks if this array is equal to another array element-wise. Returns: An array of boolean values indicating equality at each position
- `func isGreaterThan(_ value: Element) -> [Bool]` — Checks if each element in this array is greater than the specified value. Returns: An array of boolean values
- `func isLessThan(_ value: Element) -> [Bool]` — Checks if each element in this array is less than the specified value. Returns: An array of boolean values
- `func isGreaterThanOrEqual(_ value: Element) -> [Bool]` — Checks if each element in this array is greater than or equal to the specified value. Returns: An array of boolean values
- `func isLessThanOrEqual(_ value: Element) -> [Bool]` — Checks if each element in this array is less than or equal to the specified value. Returns: An array of boolean values

## Array extensions where Element == Bool

- `var trueIndices: [Int] { get }` — Returns the indices of all `true` elements in the boolean array. Returns: An array of integer indices where the value is `true`
- `func and(_ other: [Bool]) -> [Bool]` — Performs element-wise logical AND with another boolean array. Returns: A new boolean array where each element is `true` only if both corresponding elements are `true`
- `func or(_ other: [Bool]) -> [Bool]` — Performs element-wise logical OR with another boolean array. Returns: A new boolean array where each element is `true` if either corresponding element is `true`
- `var not: [Bool] { get }` — Returns the element-wise logical negation of the boolean array. Returns: A new boolean array where each element is inverted

## Array extensions

- `func masked(by mask: [Bool]) -> [Element]` — Returns elements where the mask is true. Returns: Array containing only elements where the mask is true
- `func maskedWithIndices(by mask: [Bool]) -> [(index: Int, value: Element)]` — Returns elements where the mask is true, along with their original indices. Returns: Array of tuples containing the original index and value for each true element *(since 1.0.1)*
- `func choose(where condition: [Bool], otherwise other: [Element]) -> [Element]` — Returns a new array with elements conditionally chosen from this array or another. Returns: Array with elements chosen conditionally from this array or other
